summary: The Cyber PIVOTT Act amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to establish education and training programs, scholarships, internships, and post-graduation service requirements aimed at building a skills-based cyber workforce through partnerships with community colleges and technical schools.

affected_groups.effect: Receive full scholarships, stipends, and certification vouchers for two-year cyber or technical programs, in exchange for a two-year post-graduation government service obligation or potential repayment liabilities.
Eligible to partner with CISA to offer the PIVOTT Program, conduct skills-based exercises, place interns, and monitor student compliance.
affected_groups.group: Community colleges, technical schools, and two-year higher education institutions

affected_groups.effect: Gain access to a pipeline of trained cyber interns and graduates fulfilling their two-year post-graduation service obligations.
affected_groups.group: Federal, State, local, Tribal, and territorial governments

affected_groups.effect: Required to administer scholarships, coordinate internships, secure background checks and clearances, manage outreach, and meet enrollment and reporting targets.

key_provisions: Establishes the PIVOTT Program to partner with community colleges, technical schools, and two-year higher education institutions to provide cyber education, training, internships, and job opportunities.
Provides students participating in the Program with full tuition scholarships, academic and lab fees, travel, lodging, stipends, and certification testing fees.
Imposes a two-year service obligation for program graduates to work in a cyber or cyber-relevant role for an executive agency or a State, local, Tribal, or territorial government.
Requires students to complete a minimum of four eligible skills-based exercises (such as laboratory work, hackathons, or table-top exercises) with at least one completed in-person.
Mandates specific enrollment growth targets, starting with no fewer than 250 students in the first full academic year and scaling up over subsequent years.
Requires CISA to maintain an online database of cyber training resources and job opportunities, and to establish a certification program funded via student vouchers.
Requires the Director of CISA to submit a review of existing CISA education and training programs and their resource gaps to Congress within 90 days.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Cyber PIVOTT Act amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to establish education and training programs, scholarships, internships, and post-graduation service requirements aimed at building a skills-based cyber workforce through partnerships with community colleges and technical schools.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a structured federal pipeline for cybersecurity talent focusing on two-year and technical institutions, committing federal resources to scholarships and training while mandating public-sector service obligations.
